cities.d: the country's capital, on Grande Comore

x.around: There is no bus service in Moroni; everyone travels within the city by shared taxi. You can stop a taxi anywhere in the city and ask if your destination matches with the driver's route. A ride within the city costs CF200 per person, CF250 for further destinations like Iconi or Itsandra and no more than CF500 to the airport.

hidden.d: Established in 1989, this national museum has four exhibit rooms devoted to the preservation of Comoros' cultural heritage.
Volo Volo market is the biggest in the city, and the island. It will give you an insight into local culture and life. It's better to visit in the morning when it is bursting with energy.

x.intro: Moroni (in Arabic موروني Mūrūnī) is the capital and largest city of the Comoros. It is a lively city and an ideal base to organise trips around the island, as there are several travel agencies and you can find any kind of service you may need by asking people around. The downside is that there is a lot of garbage all over the coast, and in many other places around the city.

cities.d: second largest town of Moheli, on the southern coast

x.intro: Nioumachoua is the second-largest town in Moheli. In the south of the island, it is the base to explore Moheli Natural Park.

next.d: is a beautiful villa at the eastern point of the island, where green turtles come to bury their eggs.

intro: The Comoros (French: Comores; Arabic: جزر القمر Juzur al-Qumur) is an island nation off the coast of East Africa, in the Indian Ocean between northern Mozambique and northern Madagascar.

other.d: an active volcano and the highest peak in Comoros, famous for its crater.

x.intro: Mount Karthala is a volcano on the island of Grand Comore in the Comoros.
x.safe: The volcano is considered very active. It erupted 20 times since the 19th century, last time being 2005.
